Deploying FastAPI services

Notes on running FastAPI apps in something resembling production: process model, workers, and what belongs in front of the app server.

Running with uvicorn

Uvicorn is the ASGI server we use everywhere. For local work a single reloading process is all you need:

uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload

Never ship --reload to production — it watches the filesystem and roughly doubles memory usage for no benefit.

Multiple worker processes

A single Python process handles one CPU core. To use more cores, run multiple worker processes with the --workers flag:

uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4

Each worker is a separate process with its own memory and its own copy of anything you loaded at startup — including in-process caches and ML models, so four workers means four copies of the model in RAM. A common starting point is one worker per core, then adjust from measurements. In container platforms that scale by replicas (Kubernetes, most PaaS), prefer one worker per container and let the orchestrator handle the fan-out — two schedulers fighting over the same cores helps nobody.

Reverse proxy in front

Terminate TLS and buffer slow clients in a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, or the platform's ingress), not in uvicorn. The proxy handles header sanitisation and request size limits; pass --proxy-headers to uvicorn so the app sees the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For.

Health checks

Expose a cheap /health endpoint that returns 200 without touching the database. Load balancers poll it every few seconds; making it do real work turns your health check into a small self-inflicted load test.
